task.title: Fix payment client timeouts
task.description: Payment requests intermittently time out under load. Propose a safe fix consistent with the existing retry constraints.

proposal.summary: Propose a bounded, idempotency-safe payment-client fix for intermittent load-related timeouts, without changing payment semantics or exceeding existing retry constraints. No project records were provided in the task input, so current numeric limits are not asserted.
plan_steps: Review the stored timeout, connection-pool, and retry records before changing any numeric values
Adjust timeout or pool settings only within documented limits and keep the existing retry cap
Retry only idempotent timeouts with exponential backoff and jitter
Add timeout, pool-wait, and retry metrics and roll out gradually with rollback criteria

claims.statement: Payment requests must not be retried after a timeout unless the request carries an idempotency key, to avoid duplicate payment submission.
This fix does not increase the number of payment-client retry attempts beyond the existing documented retry limit and does not introduce unlimited retries.
This fix changes only payment-client timeout, connection pooling or reuse, and retry timing; it does not change payment payloads, endpoints, or payment semantics.

assumptions: Timeouts are correlated with load-related latency or connection contention, so increasing client timeout headroom, connection reuse, or pool capacity is expected to reduce timeouts; this causal expectation was not provided in the task input.
Exponential backoff with jitter is expected to reduce synchronized retry load compared with immediate retries.
uncertainties: No stored records were provided: current request/connect timeout values, connection-pool limits, maximum retry attempts, backoff parameters, and idempotency support are unknown.
The recorded cause of the timeouts under load — downstream latency, pool exhaustion, thread limits, or network saturation — is not provided.
Whether any payment operations are documented as non-retryable regardless of idempotency is not provided.

evidence.content: Constraint: outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter; unbounded retries caused the 2026-08 outage.
Fact: the payment-client default RetryPolicy is max_attempts = 1 with jitter_ms = 0, so a single transient upstream timeout surfaces to users as a payment timeout.
Fact: in the 2026-08 outage, retry bursts from payment clients amplified an upstream slowdown into a full outage.
Fact: send_with_retries in payment-client retries only SendError::Timeout, up to RetryPolicy.max_attempts; upstream errors are returned at once without a retry.
Decision (2026-09 payments review): fix payment timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts = 3 with jitter_ms of at least 50; raising the attempt cap above 3 is not allowed.
Fact: payment client timeouts correlate with retry bursts above 5 attempts.
Fact: the payment-client test constraint_cap_is_three_attempts fails for any RetryPolicy with max_attempts above 3 or with jitter_ms equal to 0.

items.description: The plan to keep the existing retry cap conflicts with the documented current default of max_attempts=1 and the decision to set max_attempts=3, so the proposal either leaves the single-attempt timeout failure in place or mischaracterizes an increase from 1 to 3 as keeping the existing cap.

The proposal provides no numeric max_attempts or jitter_ms commitment and no plan to run constraint_cap_is_three_attempts, even though that test fails for max_attempts above 3 or jitter_ms equal to 0 and the decision requires jitter_ms of at least 50.

Claim-2 is unsupported because send_with_retries is documented as retrying SendError::Timeout up to max_attempts with no documented idempotency-key check, and no retrieved record establishes that payment requests carry keys or that downstream processing deduplicates keyed retries.

The proposal does not reconcile Claim-2's idempotency-key precondition with the documented decision to fix timeouts by setting the payment-client RetryPolicy to max_attempts=3, which states no such precondition.

Claim-4 is unsupported for the timeout and connection-pool parts of the plan because the retrieved records document only RetryPolicy attempts and jitter limits and provide no timeout values, pool limits, or documented basis for pool changes.

The proposed exponential backoff does not match the documented RetryPolicy controls, which are described in terms of max_attempts and jitter_ms, and the proposal does not specify the required jitter_ms floor of at least 50.

The proposal lacks concrete retry-burst or rollback thresholds to contain load amplification, even though retry bursts were documented to amplify an upstream slowdown into the 2026-08 outage and outbound retries must be capped at 3 attempts with jitter.

assessments.note: No Valid record states an idempotency-key precondition, that payment requests carry keys, or that downstream processing deduplicates keyed retries. Record 161896895843658017381255677281559699870 describes retrying SendError::Timeout up to max_attempts with no idempotency check, and record 328114099256634798832222840773545327795 sets max_attempts=3 without that precondition.

The proposal commits to no numeric max_attempts or jitter_ms. Record 287567405605917891851290763137356115373 states the default is max_attempts=1, while record 328114099256634798832222840773545327795 directs max_attempts=3, conflicting with describing the change as simply keeping the existing cap and not verifying compliance with the documented limit.

No Valid record provides timeout values, connection-pool limits, or states that payloads, endpoints, or payment semantics remain unchanged; the records document only RetryPolicy attempts and jitter, and the proposal specifies no jitter_ms floor.
